subject: Clarifying data-fence expectations: Dedicated vs Private VPC for MedSyn POC
body:
From: Asha Mehta <asha@medsyn.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jasdeep Singh <jasdeep.singh@medsyn.com>, procurement@medsyn.com
Date: Sat, 22 Mar 2025 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment isolation expectations and next steps

Thanks for the time earlier today — quick recap and two clarifying asks from our side. High level: MedSyn is running a small POC for our clinical summarization workflow; security needs are the gating factor.

What we captured on the call:
- We want to avoid any shared-tenant data plane for PHI at any point.
- Preference is private control plane + VPC peering where model inference runs in a customer-managed VPC (on our AWS account); fallback is dedicated Redwood capacity if VPC/on-prem proves infeasible.
- KMS residency: keys must be in our AWS account and HSM-backed is preferred.
- Logs: audit events for inference requests must be exportable to our Splunk with <24h retention in our retention tier.

Two clarifying asks before we finalize the mutual action plan:
1) From Redwood’s perspective, what exact controls differ between Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool in Redwood tenancy) vs Private VPC (model runtime in our AWS account)? Specifically: network egress paths, KMS integ, and access to raw input tokens/temporary caches.
2) If we need the private VPC option, what is the earliest timeline you have for the private control plane + VPC peering onboarding? We’re aiming to start the POC in mid-April.

Also attaching the POC scope doc and rough timeline.

Thanks,
Asha
--
Asha Mehta
VP, Engineering
MedSyn Health

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Mehta <asha@medsyn.com>
Cc: Jasdeep Singh <jasdeep.singh@medsyn.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, procurement@medsyn.com
Date: Mon, 24 Mar 2025 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment isolation expectations and next steps

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear notes and the POC scope. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps.

Summary answer (short):
- Dedicated capacity: Redwood hosts the inference runtime in our tenancy on dedicated GPU pools. Data plane isolation is enforced at tenant and process level; however control plane and some operational telemetry remain in Redwood-managed services. KMS can be customer-supplied via BYOK with keys in your AWS account for encryption at rest, but TLS session keys and some ephemeral caching keys live in Redwood runtime.
- Private VPC (VPC peering / customer VPC): Runtime and model artifacts run in your AWS account under an AMI/container we supply. Control plane calls (management/rollouts) can be proxied via private control plane options; customer KMS (BYOK) and HSM are fully supported. Network egress is controlled by you — we do not route data through Redwood tenancy.

Key differences to call out (detailed):
- Network egress and routing: On Dedicated, egress control is ours with firewall rules and NATs in Redwood account; we provide the ability to whitelist destination IPs and export logs, but IP ownership remains with Redwood. On Private VPC, all egress flows are under your AWS networking and peering; Redwood has no direct internet egress unless you configure cross-account routes.
- KMS & secrets: Both modes support BYOK; Private VPC lets keys remain inside your account and HSM. Dedicated supports BYOK for model-at-rest encryption; however some ephemeral keys used by runtime caching are managed by Redwood unless you enable customer-side cache gateways (requires additional ops integration).
- Access to raw tokens/KV caches: Dedicated runtime minimizes persistence and follows our redaction rules; we can sign an SP to restrict access, but the runtime process still executes in Redwood-managed infra. Private VPC ensures the KV cache never leaves your account unless you enable remote telemetry exports.
- Audit logs & observability: We can stream request-level audit events to your Splunk in both modes. In Private VPC, the webhook/source is from your VPC so ingestion is direct. On Dedicated, logs are exported from Redwood-managed collectors (we can push to your Splunk collector over a private connection).

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben (cc’d) to share a short one-pager matrix (Dedicated vs Private VPC) with exact controls and boolean flags for the items above + an appendix for the engineering checklist.
2) Soojin will scope the compliance evidence we can commit for the POC (SOC2 sections, encryption, audit export proof).
3) If you confirm Private VPC is required, we’ll raise a ticket to onboard your AWS account and propose an initial runbook; estimated lead time today is ~3–4 weeks for basic onboarding, faster for a simplified POC.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call Wednesday to decide which mode to start the POC in? Mid-April start is doable but tight for Private VPC unless we fast-track onboarding.

Attaching the POC schedule you sent — will follow up with Ben’s one-pager by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pr iya_natarajan@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Asha Mehta <asha@medsyn.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jasdeep Singh <jasdeep.singh@medsyn.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Mar 2025 17:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment isolation expectations and next steps

Hi all — attaching the Dedicated-vs-Private-VPC_Controls matrix (tabbed) and a brief KMS residency note. Key practical points from engineering: 

- For the POC, if you want zero possibility of token data leaving your account, Private VPC (runtime in customer account) is the only way to guarantee that. That said, Dedicated with strict tenancy + contractual clauses plus a short retention window is commonly acceptable for customers who cannot run in their VPC.
- Private VPC onboarding steps we’ll need from MedSyn: AWS account id + account owner contact, list of VPC subnets to use, IAM role we can assume (minimal privileges), and a KMS key ARN for BYOK. Estimate 2–3 business days of Redwood ENG time to provision and smoke-test once we have those items.
- If procurement needs a clear SOW for private control plane work, we can draft one — typical SOW for initial onboarding is 40 hours of eng + runbook and test harness.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-config.xlsx (controls matrix), kms-residency-brief.pdf

Short technical footnote: We keep KV caches encrypted and ephemeral by default; cache pages exist in memory only and are not persisted to disk unless you enable a shared cache layer (which you would not do for this POC).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 25 Mar 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment isolation expectations and next steps

Thanks — that was incredibly helpful and clearer than the call. A couple confirmations from our side: 
- We agree Private VPC is the desired target for the POC to ensure data plane residency in our account.
- We will share AWS account id, KMS ARN, and VPC subnet list by EOD Wednesday.
- Procurement requests SOW estimate for the 40 hours onboarding + any success criteria language; I’ll loop procurement on this thread.

A quick ask: can Ben add an explicit line in the controls matrix about ephemeral token handling and whether any debugging tools might surface tokens in logs (we want confirmation that tokens are redacted from any debug output auto-uploads)?

If you can confirm the 2–3 business day smoke-test SLA after we hand over the AWS details, we’ll lock a start date for the POC on April 14.

Best,
Asha

Attachments referenced: MedSyn-POC-scope.pdf
